decks.module: Leaving a vehicle on the road
decks.domain: Emergency and prohibited parking, freeway entry and exit, lane use, gore areas, freeway stops, HOV lanes and freeway restrictions

cards.front: Where should you stop if you must leave your vehicle on a highway or street?
cards.back: If you must leave your vehicle on a highway or street, pull onto the shoulder as far from traffic as you can, or as close to the curb as possible where there is one.
cards.memory_hook: far off, or at the curb

cards.front: What should you do to secure the vehicle before leaving it?
cards.back: Before leaving it, set the parking brake, shift into park or leave a manual transmission in gear, and switch off the engine.

cards.front: What should you put out, and where should you stay, after leaving a vehicle on the road?
cards.back: Put out proper emergency signals and, if possible, stay with the vehicle until help arrives.

cards.front: What should you do if you must walk away from the vehicle?
cards.back: If you have to walk away from the vehicle, lock it.

decks.domain: Emergency and prohibited parking, freeway entry and exit, lane use, gore areas, freeway stops, HOV lanes and freeway restrictions

cards.front: Which three places does the manual name where parking is illegal?
cards.back: Parking is illegal on a sidewalk, in front of any public or private driveway, and inside the boundaries of an intersection.

cards.front: How close to a crosswalk at an intersection may you not park?
cards.back: Parking is illegal on a crosswalk, and also anywhere closer than twenty feet to a crosswalk at an intersection.

cards.front: When may you park on a freeway or interstate?
cards.back: Parking on any freeway or interstate highway is illegal except in an emergency.

cards.front: If you must stop on a freeway in an emergency, do the usual stopping steps still apply?
cards.back: Freeway parking is banned except for emergencies, and an emergency stop still calls for the shoulder, the brake, the engine off and warning signals.

cards.front: What else makes parking illegal besides the listed places?
cards.back: You may not park where signs prohibit it or in any way that creates a hazard for other vehicles.

cards.front: How close to a fire hydrant is parking illegal?
cards.back: Parking within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant is illegal.

cards.front: How close to a railroad crossing is parking illegal?
cards.back: Parking within fifty feet of a railroad crossing is illegal.

cards.front: How do the no-parking distances for hydrants, crosswalks and railroad crossings differ?
cards.back: The no-parking distances differ by object: fifteen feet from a fire hydrant, twenty feet from a crosswalk at an intersection, and fifty feet from a railroad crossing.

cards.front: May you park on a bridge or inside a tunnel?
cards.back: You may not park on a bridge or inside a tunnel.

decks.domain: Emergency and prohibited parking, freeway entry and exit, lane use, gore areas, freeway stops, HOV lanes and freeway restrictions

cards.front: What are freeways and interstate highways built for?
cards.back: Freeways and interstate highways are built to carry higher-speed traffic safely.

cards.front: Who must yield when a driver enters a freeway?
cards.back: Drivers entering a freeway must yield to the traffic already on it and are responsible for merging safely.

cards.front: How do you merge onto a freeway?
cards.back: To merge, match your speed to the traffic in the freeway's right lane, signal, check the traffic around you and merge carefully once it is clear.

cards.front: What must you not cross or drive through while entering a freeway?
cards.back: While entering a freeway, do not cross a solid line or drive through a gore area.

cards.front: Which areas are off-limits when entering and exiting a freeway?
cards.back: A solid line is off-limits both when entering and when exiting a freeway, and so is the gore area on entry.

cards.front: What should you do before exiting a freeway?
cards.back: Signal before you exit a freeway.

cards.front: What helps you exit most freeways smoothly?
cards.back: Most freeways have deceleration lanes to help you exit, and proper braking gives a smooth exit.

cards.front: How does freeway entry differ from freeway exit in speed?
cards.back: On entry you match the speed of the freeway right lane, while on exit most freeways give you a deceleration lane in which to brake smoothly.

cards.front: How should you exit in heavy traffic?
cards.back: When exiting in heavy traffic, keep a space cushion behind the vehicle ahead and do not cross a solid line.

decks.domain: Emergency and prohibited parking, freeway entry and exit, lane use, gore areas, freeway stops, HOV lanes and freeway restrictions

cards.front: What is a divided highway or freeway?
cards.back: A divided highway or freeway has separate roadways for the two directions, often with several lanes on each side.

cards.front: How do controlled-access highways differ from highways with traffic signals?
cards.back: Some highways meet other roads at traffic signals, while controlled-access highways have no signals or intersections and are entered and left only by ramps; these are called expressways or freeways.

cards.front: When should you get into the proper lane for entering or leaving a highway?
cards.back: Get into the proper lane well in advance so you can enter or leave the highway safely.

cards.front: When should you signal your exit from a highway?
cards.back: Signal your exit before you reach the exit ramp.

cards.front: What should you do when joining a highway?
cards.back: When joining a highway, yield to drivers already on it and speed up to match their speed as you enter the travel lane.

cards.front: What should you do if you miss your exit?
cards.back: If you miss your exit, do not stop and never back up; leave at the next exit and follow the signs to rejoin the road going the other way.

cards.front: How should you handle a missed exit?
cards.back: A missed exit is handled by driving on to the next exit and following signs back, never by stopping or reversing.

cards.front: What must you do if you miss a freeway exit?
cards.back: If you miss a freeway exit, do not back up; you must go on to the next exit.

cards.front: Which half of a multi-lane road should you drive on?
cards.back: On any road with two or more lanes, drive on the right half except when passing or when signs say otherwise.

cards.front: Why may the right lane of a three-lane highway move slower or faster?
cards.back: On highways with three or more lanes in one direction, the right lane usually serves entering and exiting traffic, so it may move slower or faster than the other lanes.

cards.front: Why can the right lane carry traffic both slower and faster than others?
cards.back: The right lane of a highway with three or more lanes can carry traffic both slower and faster than the other lanes, because it serves entering and exiting vehicles.

cards.front: At rush hour, why may through drivers stay out of the right lane?
cards.back: At rush hour, drivers who are not exiting may want to stay out of the right lane to leave room for vehicles entering and leaving.

cards.front: What four habits does the manual list for highway lanes?
cards.back: Watch for vehicles merging into your lane, signal your own lane changes, keep within posted speed limits and do not tailgate.

cards.front: What is a gore area, and what does the law forbid there?
cards.back: Driving over or parking on any part of a gore area, the space between a through roadway and an entrance or exit ramp, is against the law.

cards.front: What exactly is the gore area?
cards.back: A gore area is the wedge between the through road and a ramp; driving over it and parking in it are both against the law.

cards.front: Where should you pull over if you need help on a freeway?
cards.back: If you need help on a freeway, pull as far as you can onto the right shoulder and avoid stopping on or near the ramps.

cards.front: How can you signal for help on a freeway?
cards.back: To signal for help, turn on your emergency flashers or raise the hood; after dark, switch on the inside dome light or set out flares or portable warning signals.

cards.front: How do help signals differ by day and after dark?
cards.back: By day you signal for freeway help with flashers or a raised hood, while after dark you add the dome light or flares and portable warning signals.

cards.front: What should you do while waiting for help on a freeway?
cards.back: Wait for help with your vehicle and do not walk along the freeway.

cards.front: What should you do when you come upon a disabled vehicle on the freeway?
cards.back: When you come upon a disabled vehicle on the freeway, slow down, move over and pass around it with caution.

decks.domain: Emergency and prohibited parking, freeway entry and exit, lane use, gore areas, freeway stops, HOV lanes and freeway restrictions

cards.front: How are HOV lanes marked?
cards.back: HOV lanes are marked by white diamonds painted in the roadway.

cards.front: Who may use an HOV lane during its posted weekday times?
cards.back: At the posted times on weekdays, a vehicle carrying fewer than two persons, counting the driver, may not use an HOV lane, which is then reserved for car pools, motorcycles and buses.

cards.front: Does the HOV two-person rule count the driver, and when does it apply?
cards.back: The HOV rule counts the driver as one of the two persons required, and it binds only at the posted weekday times.

cards.front: What happens to a motorist who breaks the HOV restriction?
cards.back: A motorist who breaks the HOV restriction faces substantial fines and penalties.

cards.front: What should you do when crossing into or out of an HOV lane?
cards.back: Always signal and take care when crossing the solid white line into or out of an HOV lane.

cards.front: Which vehicles may use an HOV lane during restricted times, and how do you cross its line?
cards.back: Car pools, motorcycles and buses may use an HOV lane during restricted times, and crossing its solid white line requires a signal.

cards.front: Which two moves are never allowed across a freeway median?
cards.back: On a freeway, never drive over or across a median or divided-highway separation, and never make a U-turn.

cards.front: How must you change lanes and get onto a freeway?
cards.back: On a freeway, never change lanes without signaling, and get onto the freeway only by an on-ramp.

cards.front: Where may you stop or park on a freeway?
cards.back: Do not park or stop on a freeway except in areas provided for it; parking on the shoulder is banned except in an emergency.

cards.front: How does the freeway shoulder rule differ from where stopping is allowed?
cards.back: Shoulder parking on a freeway is banned except in an emergency, while stopping is allowed only in areas specially provided.

cards.front: What should you check before highway driving?
cards.back: Before highway driving, make sure your vehicle is in good operating condition and can keep up highway speeds.

cards.front: Which lane is for passing, and how are three-lane highways used?
cards.back: Keep right and use the left lane only to pass; on a three-lane highway, treat the far right lane as the slower through lane and the far left lane as the passing lane.

cards.front: On a three-lane highway, what are the far right and far left lanes for?
cards.back: On a three-lane highway the far right lane is treated as the slower through lane and the far left lane as the passing lane.

cards.front: Where in your lane should you drive, and what do you use to change lanes?
cards.back: Drive in the middle of your lane between the lines, and use your rearview mirror and turn signals when changing lanes.

cards.front: What controls traffic, and why must you understand it?
cards.back: Traffic is controlled by signal lights, traffic signs and pavement markings, and you must fully understand them to drive safely.

recaps.module: Leaving a vehicle on the road

recap_hooks.text: To leave a vehicle on the road, pull well off, secure it, put out emergency signals, stay with it if you can, and lock it if you walk away.
Keep fifteen feet from a hydrant, twenty from a crosswalk at an intersection, and fifty from a railroad crossing.
Never park on a freeway except in an emergency.
Yield and match speed to merge on, signal and use the deceleration lane to exit, and never cross a solid line.
Get into your lane early, keep to the right half, and if you miss an exit, go on to the next one.
Stay out of the gore area, and if you need help, pull far onto the right shoulder, signal and wait with the car.
White diamonds mark HOV lanes, the driver counts toward the two persons, and you signal across the solid line.
On a freeway, no median crossings, no U-turns, no stopping except in provided areas, and keep right except to pass.
